paragraphs: Stellic makes software for colleges and universities that turns the route to a degree into something a student can actually see and an office can support. It pitches itself across the range of institution types, from large public schools and community colleges to small private and research universities.

One package tracks degree progress and gives students room to plan ahead. One is built for advisors, giving them a way to step in early rather than after a student has fallen behind. A third is aimed at transfer and prospective students, matching them to a path based on goals and the credits they already carry. Transcript processing is automated to cut manual data entry.

The company says it has supported over a million students so far. It describes itself as a partner to schools of every size. The platform is named for Mark Stehlik, the advisor who helped the founders picture the system while they were still students. The site also states that the product is certified for accessibility.

quote.text: Stellic turns academic planning into a path every student can see and every office can support, all the way to graduation.
